maria_cho: Heads-up — saw a cluster of RX/TX error bursts on p5zn instances in us-west-2 after last night's NIC firmware rollout. Affected pods saw degraded east-west throughput and some short-lived reconnects.
noah_lin: I can confirm. Metrics: rx_errors jumped ~3 orders of magnitude 00:12-00:18 UTC. Packet loss ~0.6% on the internal gRPC path.
noah_lin: Quick grep from one host: ```sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_no_buffer'``` returned lots of rx_no_buffer and rx_crc_errors.
sasha_k: Which driver/firmware combo did the rollout push?
infra-bot: Deploy finished: nic-fw-rollout-2026-03-17 v1.2.7 -> applied to fleet segment p5zn-usw2-azb (job id d3f9).
maria_cho: firmware v1.2.7, driver still mlx5 5.15. We pushed the firmware because it fixed a different jitter issue on c7gn. Looks like p5zn reacts poorly.
noah_lin: On a suspect host I tried toggling MTU (9000 -> 1500) and errors drop significantly. Could be MTU negotiation / path MSS mismatch combined with new firmware's RX buffer tuning.
sasha_k: Interesting — did the rollout change any offload flags? TCP segmentation offload (TSO)/GSO changes can surface as rx_no_buffer when MTU expectations differ.
maria_cho: We didn't explicitly change offload config, but firmware release notes mention "adaptive ring sizes and coalescing".
noah_lin: Quick logs: ```Mar 17 00:14 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0 enp134s0f0: mlx5e: FALLBACK: rx queue 7 error: -110```
ops-oncall: Can we roll back the firmware on a canary AZ first? Don't want to blast rollback across the whole region yet.
sasha_k: Agreed. Plan: 1) isolate a small canary pool (10 instances) in us-west-2b, 2) revert firmware to v1.2.5, 3) monitor rx_errors and gRPC latency for 30m. If clean, expand.
maria_cho: I'll open a deployment window. Also adding a temporary automatic MTU mitigation: set kube CNI host-mtu override to 1500 for affected node group to reduce packet fragmentation while we validate.
noah_lin: How about RDMA paths? Any impact there? p5zn has kernel rdma support — I saw no rdma_dev timeouts but we should check ibv_cq errors.
sasha_k: Run this on hosts with SR-IOV enabled: ```dmesg | egrep 'rdma|ib|mlx5' -n | tail -30``` and capture next 30m. If RDMA stays clean, it points more to L2 coalescing.
infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INFRA-2026-427 (p5zn us-west-2 RX error surge). Assigned: eng-infra oncall.
ops-oncall: I'll kick off the canary rollback in 10m and attach results here. Also notifying support to hold Dedicated capacity expansions in us-west-2 until we green. :warning:
maria_cho: Thanks. If rollback shows improvement, we should mark v1.2.7 as problematic for p5zn and update release notes to block auto-apply to p5zn instance pools.
noah_lin: One more data point: tcpdump showed lots of TCP retransmits consistent with RX buffer exhaustion. Temporary kernel knob we can try: `sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=16777216` on nodes — might blunt impact while rollback runs.
sasha_k: Ok leaving action items: canary rollback, MTU host override, sysctl bump on canary, capture ethtool stats pre/post. Keep replies short and paste logs.
maria_cho: Will post canary results in ~25m. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
